transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Nora Diaz (Canterra Head of Platform), Evan Rossi (Security Engineer), Priya Shah (Director, ML), Samir Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro from our side — i'm Maya, AE on this account, and Liam is our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:07] Nora (Canterra): good, thanks. busy day but excited to dig in.
[00:11] Liam (Redwood): hi, everyone — quick agenda, we'll run through Canterra's security and hosting constraints, high-level options (hosted/dedicated/private), then dig into SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS. we can leave time for benchmarks and next steps.
[00:23] Priya (Canterra): sounds good. main thing for us is PII handling — we have consumer payments and need to be conservative.
[00:29] Evan (Canterra): yep, SOC two and ISO are table stakes for procurement. also KMS integration is a must, and we'd like customer-managed keys if possible.
[00:38] Maya (Redwood): totally understood. to set expectations: Redwood supports hosted with strict tenancy isolation, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC / on-prem). For high compliance customers we recommend Private so the control plane and data plane are entirely in your VPC — but we can walk through tradeoffs.
[00:50] Samir (Canterra): can you clarify what you mean by "control plane" for Private — is it still Redwood-managed or fully customer-managed?
[00:58] Liam (Redwood): good question. for our Private offering the control plane can be run in a customer VPC with limited Redwood access patterns — there are two flavors: managed private (we deploy but network-restricted) and air-gapped on-prem where you host everything. in both cases logs, audit trails, and keys stay under your KMS if you choose CMK integration. sometimes our docs call this "private control plane" which confuses people.
[01:18] Nora (Canterra): would that satisfy our procurement team? they ask for evidence — SOC2, ISO certs, and an attestation on log retention.
[01:25] Maya (Redwood): yes — we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 summary under NDA. we'll also provide our architecture diagram for Private deployments and the audit logging controls. i'll attach our compliance pack.
[01:34] Evan (Canterra): when you say "attach" — is there a process? our security team needs to validate the report and sometimes requests a contact at audit firm.
[01:41] Maya (Redwood): we can share the PDF report and a contact — typically procurement does a short validation call with our security team or auditor.
[01:46] Priya (Canterra): on the technical side: how do you do encryption in transit and at rest? and can we bring our HSM?
[01:52] Liam (Redwood): encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3 across the board. at rest we support cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and key wrapping with customer-managed keys (CMKs). for on-prem or air-gapped, you can integrate with an HSM via PKCS#11 or a proxy. note some of the vendor-specific drivers require network egress for rotation callbacks, so we usually design a rotation proxy.
[02:14] Speaker 1 (Canterra, unclear): you mentioned CMK — who actually holds the key material?
[02:18] Liam (Redwood): if you select CMK in your KMS, you retain control — Redwood only gets encrypted blobs. for Hosted we can offer bring-your-key with envelope encryption; but there are caveats if you want zero-knowledge — that pushes you to Private/on-prem.
[02:33] Nora (Canterra): ok. what about SSO? we run SAML via Azure AD and want SCIM for provisioning.
[02:38] Maya (Redwood): we support SAML2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. role syncs via SCIM plus RBAC in the Console — you can map groups to roles. we also have session controls and MFA hooks.
[02:51] Evan (Canterra): audit logs — how granular? we need immutable logs of model access, prompting, and who requested inference, plus ability to export to our SIEM (Splunk).
[02:59] Liam (Redwood): logs include token-level access events, model version, route, request/response metadata (we redact full responses by default for privacy), and admin actions like role changes. exports via syslog/S3 ingestion to your SIEM are supported. retention configurable per deployment, and for Dedicated/Private you can set longer retention and archival policies.
[03:17] Priya (Canterra): redact full responses by default — can we opt out for certain service accounts? we have internal teams that need raw outputs for evals.
[03:24] Liam (Redwood): yes, you can whitelist service accounts and route their outputs to a secure bucket with stricter access controls. that would be in the Dedicated/Private realm usually.
[03:32] [03:33] Nora (Canterra): any certifications for the dedicated infra?
[03:35] Maya (Redwood): Dedicated nodes run in our cloud account but with project isolation and hardened images — they fall under our SOC2 umbrella. for extra assurance we can do customer-specific pen test reviews on the provisioned environment.
[03:46] Samir (Canterra): latency is important. our product team wants sub-200ms 95th for short prompts. how does Dedicated vs Hosted compare?
[03:54] Liam (Redwood): Dedicated gives more predictable p95 latency since you have reserved resources and we can tune batching/queues. Hosted is multi-tenant and optimized but subject to burst policy and routing. Private on-prem will give you lowest network variance but you take on ops. there's a cost-latency tradeoff. we can run a short benchmark with your sample to quantify.
[04:14] Priya (Canterra): what's the overhead for KV cache / prefix caching? our use is chat with a lot of context.
[04:20] Liam (Redwood): we have KV cache and automatic prefix caching to reduce repeated token work. caching is supported across Dedicated and Private. Hosted offers some caching but with stricter eviction to protect multi-tenant fairness. sometimes the cache naming shows up as "K V cache" in docs; sorry transcription typos are common.
[04:36] Evan (Canterra): retention policy — we have regulatory 7-year retention on certain records. can Redwood meet long-term archival?
[04:42] Maya (Redwood): for Dedicated and Private you can push audit logs and redacted transcripts to your S3/GCS archival with lifecycle to Glacier/Coldline for 7+ years. Hosted can do export but long-term retention is managed by you if you accept the export flow; Redwood’s hosted retention defaults are shorter, so we recommend Dedicated/Private for multi-year regulatory retention.
[05:01] Nora (Canterra): procurement also wants an IP & data residency statement — we operate primarily in CA and EU. can you guarantee region pinning?
[05:09] Liam (Redwood): yes for Dedicated and Private we can pin regions. Hosted API also supports region routing for paid tiers but it's not a hard physical boundary like a VPC. we'll provide the residency diagram in the compliance pack.
[05:20] Priya (Canterra): any guest/third-party access? some vendors ask for a maintenance window where Redwood engineers might need access.
[05:27] Maya (Redwood): for Private we can limit or not allow Redwood direct access; for Managed Private we do ask for emergency access with strict JIT and SOC approvals. all access is audited.
[05:36] Evan (Canterra): do you do annual pen tests and vulnerability scans?
[05:40] Maya (Redwood): yes we have quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party pen tests; summary results available in our compliance repo.
[05:47] [05:48] Speaker 2 (Priya): is there support for data masking or PII scrubbing before storage?
[05:52] Liam (Redwood): we provide PII detection pipelines and optional masking plugins — common pattern is client-side PII stripping before sending to the API or server-side redaction with rules. for the highest compliance we recommend client-side or Private with local redaction.
[06:06] Nora (Canterra): thinking about timeline — we want to pilot with a subset of traffic in Q1 and go to prod by end of Q2. any constraints?
[06:13] Maya (Redwood): that timeline is feasible. pilot usually starts on Hosted or Dedicated trial, then we transition to Private for full production if required. key gating factors: legal review of SOC2 docs, KMS integration sign-off, and bench results.
[06:25] Evan (Canterra): cost question — if we do Private, is pricing fixed or usage-based plus infra?
[06:30] Maya (Redwood): Private is a platform license plus infra ops — model is hybrid: baseline platform fee for Private plus per-token or per-instance usage depending on the arrangement. Dedicated is reserved capacity with committed monthly cost. we can put numbers in the next doc.
[06:42] Liam (Redwood): also worth pointing out Optimize features — intelligent batching and quant recommendations to reduce unit cost while hitting latency SLOs. that's especially useful for Dedicated.
[06:51] Priya (Canterra): ok, on SAML — we need group-to-role mapping and SCIM provisioning. what's the typical setup time?
[06:58] Maya (Redwood): usually 1-2 weeks for SAML and SCIM once we have a test account and your IdP metadata; for Dedicated/Private it's similar but we sometimes need additional network config.
[07:08] Samir (Canterra): are audit logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody assurances for legal.
[07:13] Liam (Redwood): we support append-only logs and can publish digests to an external ledger occasionally. for Private, you can ingest logs into your immutable storage with custody controls. we do JWS signing of critical admin actions.
[07:26] Nora (Canterra): any blockers on bringing our HSM on AWS?
[07:30] Liam (Redwood): not usually — AWS KMS CMKs are supported; if you require an external HSM with PKCS#11, we'll validate driver compatibility. rotation semantics may need a short window.
[07:41] Priya (Canterra): one more: data deletion / right to be forgotten — can you fulfill deletion requests downstream?
[07:47] Maya (Redwood): for Dedicated/Private we can delete customer-specific datasets and revoke keys which renders stored blobs unreadable. For Hosted we honor deletion but need to follow retention for audit logs; we can provide deletion certificates.
[07:59] Evan (Canterra): are there SLA uptime numbers for Dedicated?
[08:02] Maya (Redwood): Dedicated comes with SLA commitments — we'll include the SLA doc, p99/p95 objectives, and incident response commitments in the package.
[08:10] Liam (Redwood): quick note — some terminology in our docs is rough, e.g., "redwood-dedicated" vs "dedicated capacity" — i'll make a clear doc mapping to avoid confusion.
[08:18] [08:19] Nora (Canterra): thanks. is there a demo or PoC we can do that shows keys, audit logs, and region pinning?
[08:25] Maya (Redwood): yes — next step: we propose a short PoC: 2-3 days to wire SCIM/SAML, test KMS integration on a dev cluster, and run a micro-benchmark with representative payloads. we'll coordinate with your infra.
[08:36] Priya (Canterra): what would we need to provide for the bench?
[08:38] Liam (Redwood): sample prompts, typical context length distribution, expected concurrency, and a redacted dataset if possible. also your target p95 SLA to measure against.
[08:48] Evan (Canterra): i'll compile expected QPS and retention rules, and send them over.
[08:53] Maya (Redwood): perfect. i'll also share the compliance pack and our SOC 2 cert under NDA. we can set the infra deep-dive for Jan 24 if that works?
[08:59] Nora (Canterra): Jan 24 works for us.
[09:02] Maya (Redwood): great — quick recap of action items and owners.
[09:06] [09:07] Liam (Redwood): recap: share SOC2/ISO, bench plan, sample payloads, infra deep-dive next week.
[09:12] Nora (Canterra): yep — Evan will send retention policy and QPS numbers.
[09:18] Maya (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc bundle and calendar invite.
[09:22] (meeting end)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and some audio dropouts around 00:50–01:00 caused a repeated clarification. There are a few transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache, "SOC two" spelled out).
